LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 7.3.1: PERSONAL AND POSSESSIVE PRONOUNS.

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.3: Grammar in Use 7.3.1: Personal and possessive pronouns.
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 7.3.1: Personal and possessive pronouns., part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should we avoid unnecessary repetition?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. distinguish between personal and possessive pronouns in sentences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 7.3.1: Personal and possessive pronouns. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use personal and possessive pronouns in sentences appropriately,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 7.3.1: Personal and possessive pronouns. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the value of proper use of pronouns.  Pick out personal and possessive pronouns from print and non-print texts on natural resources in pairs. Learners who may not turn pages to use page-turners or be supported by peers. They could use adapted writing materials or type on appropriate adapted digital devices to record findings.  Use personal pronouns to refer to people in a class,  Construct sentences using personal pronouns, Learners Why should we avoid unnecessary repetition? 67 with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing materials or type on appropriate adapted digital devices to construct sentences.  Write a paragraph using possessive pronouns,  Construct sentences using personal pronouns from substitution and completion tables,  Draw a chart with singular/plural, subjective, and objective personal pronouns and display them for peer review.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 7.3.1: Personal and possessive pronouns. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 7.3.1: Personal and possessive pronouns. together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication is enhanced as the learner uses correct personal pronouns to construct sentences.

Values:
Respect is enhanced as the learner displays positive regard for others when using personal pronouns to construct sentences to

refer to others in class.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Social cohesion is enhanced as the learner uses personal pronouns to refer to people as they construct sentences in the class.

Link to other subjects:

The learner relates the concept of pronouns to their learning in Kiswahili.
